item.title: VoteVets Spends Millions to Elect Democrats, Shaping Midterms
item.author: Annie Karni
item.content:encoded: The organization, founded in 2006 to back Democratic veterans opposing the Iraq war, is pouring huge sums into this year’s elections amid intense voter antipathy for another conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: ‘Zombified’ C.D.C., Hobbled by Cuts, Struggles to Fulfill Scientific Mission
item.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.content:encoded: The agency has lost its independence and nearly a third of its staff, as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and associates have tightened control.

item.title: Bobby Pulido, a Texan Singer, Puts Republicans on Defense
item.author: Bayliss Wagner
item.content:encoded: Bobby Pulido, a Tejano musician running as a Democrat for the House, has left his Republican opponent struggling to match his star power in a district that President Trump won easily in 2024.

item.title: Trump and Takaichi Spoke on US-China Summit, Kyodo Says
item.author: Sam Kim
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke by phone about the US-China summit that took place earlier this week, Kyodo news agency reports.

item.title: EU Warns Members of Urgent Energy Price Crisis Before Winter Season
item.author: Ewa Krukowska
item.content:encoded: The European Union warned its member states about a potential energy price crisis driven by the Middle East conflict, asking them to consider measures to cut demand and to continue filling gas storage ahead of winter.

item.title: Runner’s Murder in South Africa Reignites Push to Stop Femicide
item.author: S'thembile Cele
item.content:encoded: Liz Ramhlola was jogging with another woman early one morning on a road bordered by vacant plots when a car slowed down beside them. The men inside opened the windows, then began jeering and arguing amongst themselves about how to “take their summer bodies.” The 37-year-old feared that she and her friend would be abducted, or worse. Eventually, the men drove away.

item.title: Poland to Pay Up to $4.4 Billion for Fort Trump, Report Says
item.author: Wojciech Moskwa
item.content:encoded: The proposed permanent US military base in Poland, dubbed Fort Trump, will cost as much as 17 billion zloty ($4.4 billion) and could open as early as in 2029, according to a report from newspaper Rzeczpospolita.

item.title: A 7-Day Standoff That Said So Much About Trump and the Media
item.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
item.content:encoded: An abrupt decree, a network boycott, a legal intervention and an uneasy détente: This was no typical battle between a president and his press corps.

item.title: Rahm Emanuel Makes His 2026 Play
item.author: Shane Goldmacher
item.content:encoded: The longtime Democratic insider has emerged as a behind-the-scenes force in his party’s push to win back Congress. After that, he’ll think about 2028.

item.title: Russia’s Ilsky Oil Refinery Ablaze After Drone Strike That Leaves Three Dead
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Ukraine said it struck the Ilsky oil refinery in Russia’s Black Sea region of Krasnodar as Kyiv maintains persistent attacks against energy infrastructure while fending off waves of drones.

item.title: The Mishal Husain Show: Qatar PM On Middle East 'Earthquake'
item.content:encoded: The Middle East is facing an “earthquake” as attacks on civilian infrastructure increasingly cross long-standing red lines, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani tells Mishal Husain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Burnham to Outline Vision for Britain’s Economy at Labour Conference
item.author: Alex Wickham, Chloe Chaplain and Joe Mayes
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham will tell the Labour Party faithful next week that he’s the leader who’ll deliver the hope and change they so badly want. The underlying message is slightly more nuanced: stick with me because things might get worse before they get better.

item.title: White House Signals It Won’t Ban Diesel Exports, Senator Says
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Nathan Risser
item.content:encoded: The White House has offered assurances that the Trump administration won’t ban US diesel exports, Senator Ted Cruz told refining industry leaders late Friday.

item.title: Houthis Attack Riyadh Again as Trump Rejects Ceasefire Offer
item.author: Dave Sebastian and Sara Gharaibeh
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia’s capital again came under attack from Yemen’s Houthis over the weekend as air raid alerts are issued on an almost daily basis in one or more areas of the kingdom.

item.title: White House Renews Media Fight, Barring CNN From Trump Trip
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: The White House is refusing to allow CNN to travel on Air Force One to cover President Donald Trump’s trip to watch a college football game in Tennessee Saturday, the network reported.

item.title: U.S. Rejects U.N. Declaration on Preparing for Future Pandemics
item.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
item.content:encoded: Most member nations spoke in support of the declaration, but some rich countries had strong objections.

item.title: Trump Proposes $810 Million in Education and Health Cuts, Defying Congress
item.author: Catie Edmondson
item.content:encoded: The attempted clawback represents the second time in as many years that the White House has sought to cancel funding approved by lawmakers.

item.title: Supreme Court Ruling Could Have Limited Impact on Voter Screening in Midterms
item.author: Richard Fausset, Nick Corasaniti and Julie Bosman
item.content:encoded: Federal law requires a 90-day “quiet period” before elections, likely restricting the immediate scope of a decision that allows the use of a citizenship database to examine voter rolls.

item.title: Supreme Court Once Again Blocks Republican-Backed Voting Map in Missouri
item.author: Ann E. Marimow and Mitch Smith
item.content:encoded: A federal appeals court had sided with Republicans seeking to use redrawn congressional district boundaries to give their party an advantage in the midterms elections.

item.title: As Xi Leaves Washington, Divisions Still Simmer Beneath the Surface
item.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs and David E. Sanger
item.content:encoded: President Trump welcomed Xi Jinping of China for a state visit that was heavy on pomp and ceremony. But surprisingly little time was spent on the issues that most divide the two superpowers.

item.title: China’s Xi Snubs a Troubled U.N. for Trump, Overshadowing Its Big Week
item.author: Michael Crowley
item.content:encoded: The U.S.-China summit offered a sharp contrast with the action at the faltering United Nations in a gridlocked New York.

item.title: Open AI Models May Have Interfered With Government Sites
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta says the state visit delivered "an awful lot of pomp, but not a lot of substance," pointing to the lack of progress on major issues between the two nations. Democratic Representative Glenn Ivey of Maryland reacts to news that OpenAI alerted more than a dozen organizations that its models may have hacked or disrupted their sites, saying Congress and the White House should be taking emerging AI risks more seriously. National Association of Manufacturers President and CEO Jay Timmons says manufacturers are looking for clearer progress on trade as President Trump and China's Xi Jinping prepare for more meetings this year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ICE Raids in Beef Country Raise Fears of Higher Prices
item.author: Kevin Draper and J. David Goodman
item.content:encoded: Cattle industry groups in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas and two Republican senators said the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement actions were hurting operations.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Open to Possibly Developing Nuclear Weapons
item.author: Julian E. Barnes and Robert Jimison
item.content:encoded: An intelligence assessment examined Saudi Arabia’s military ambitions as Congress reviews a new civilian nuclear deal between the U.S. and the kingdom.

item.title: Lula Plans $28 Billion Debt Buyout to Aid Consumers Before Vote
item.author: Martha Beck
item.content:encoded: Brazil’s government plans to spend 15 billion reais to buy as much as 150 billion reais ($28 billion) of delinquent consumer debt from banks, part of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s push to ease the financial strain on households and bolster his bid for a fourth term.

item.title: US-China Trade Needs More Stability: NAM CEO
item.content:encoded: National Association of Manufacturers President and CEO Jay Timmons says manufacturers are looking for clearer progress on trade as President Trump and China's Xi Jinping prepare for more meetings this year. He says US manufacturers remain optimistic about the outlook as orders pick up, even as tariffs, energy costs and trade uncertainty create headwinds. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ivey Calls for More Congressional Action on AI Risks
item.content:encoded: Democratic Representative Glenn Ivey of Maryland reacts to news that OpenAI alerted more than a dozen organizations that its models may have hacked or disrupted their sites, saying Congress and the White House should be taking emerging AI risks more seriously. He also discusses data-center power costs and the Democratic outlook heading into the midterms. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech, AI Leaders to Join Trump for Launch of Government Website
item.author: Courtney Subramanian
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump will host an event with tech and AI leaders on Tuesday to launch a new government website, as his administration faces pressure to adopt new guardrails for the use of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Panetta Calls Trump-Xi Summit a 'Missed Opportunity'
item.content:encoded: Former Defense Secretary Leon Panetta says the state visit delivered "an awful lot of pomp, but not a lot of substance," pointing to the lack of progress on major issues between the two nations. He also says he remains "very skeptical" that the US and Iran can reach an enforceable peace agreement before the midterms. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latest Midterm Polls Reveal Bright Spots for Republicans
item.author: Ruth Igielnik
item.content:encoded: There has been a turnaround in Maine, our new poll shows.

item.title: Supreme Court Rejects Missouri’s Republican-Drawn Voting Map
item.author: Greg Stohr and Madlin Mekelburg
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court said Missouri can’t use a Republican-drawn congressional map in the November midterm elections, resolving a complicated legal fight that has caused confusion and uncertainty over what will appear on ballots in the state.

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Trump-Xi Summit Wraps (Podcast)
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said he would meet again with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in November, following what he said was a successful summit in Washington that was seemingly light on concrete policy outcomes. Meanwhile, oil prices declined on tentative signs that talks between the US and Iran to reopen the world’s most important energy shipping route were progressing.
On today's episode: Jennifer Welch, Chief Geoeconomics Analyst for Bloomberg Economics Mekala Krishnan, Partner at the McKinsey Global Institute Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett, Permanent Representative of Guyana to the UN Rudina Seseri, Founder & Managing Partner at Glasswing Ventures (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: White House Mulls Range of Options to Lower Diesel Costs
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Ari Natter and Nathan Risser
item.content:encoded: Trump administration officials have floated a range of measures to curb soaring diesel costs, from suspending taxes on the fuel to removing restrictions on sales of a dyed, red variety normally reserved for off-road use.

item.title: Bracing for Midterm Losses, Republicans in Congress Try a Pre-election Pivot
item.author: Annie Karni and Carl Hulse
item.content:encoded: After nearly two years of allowing President Trump to set their agenda, G.O.P. senators are grasping for some quick action on cost-of-living measures they can show voters before November.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Use of Trump Administration’s Expansive Database for Voter Screening
item.author: Abbie VanSickle
item.content:encoded: Critics of a citizenship database built by the Trump administration have raised alarms about privacy and improper voter purges.

item.title: Here’s How Trump Is Building a National Citizenship Database to Check Voters
item.author: Nicholas Nehamas and Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to deploy a system that merges personal data from across the government. Questions remain about its reliability.

item.title: Xi Seizes Trump Truce to Seek Lasting Gains on Trade, Taiwan
item.author: Colum Murphy and Nectar Gan
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump’s lavish welcome of Xi Jinping this week marked a high point for stability in a US-China relationship that’s seen a lot of lows. Now, the Chinese leader is pushing to lock in more favorable terms on Taiwan and trade while he still can.

item.title: After Tough Primaries, Democrats in Key States Feel Unified, New Polls Find
item.author: Ruth Igielnik and Lisa Lerer
item.content:encoded: A majority of Democrats in Maine and Michigan said the primary process strengthened their party heading into November.

item.title: Not Long Ago, Trump Accused China of Election Meddling. Today, ‘Great Friendship.’
item.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.content:encoded: President Trump softened much of his stance toward China as he prepared to host its leader. But his disregard of a topic that has consumed him — the 2020 election — was particularly stark.

item.title: At State Dinner for China’s Leader, Melania Trump Wears the Pants
item.author: Vanessa Friedman
item.content:encoded: And possibly makes history while doing so.
